claims.statement: Every supported inference session complies as declared: one block, reading only its prompt.
claims.next: Name the calibration (session length, token coding, non-text inputs) in every headline.

claims.statement: Within one declaration with theta frozen, a compliant circuit that contains a standard dense pretraining recipe runs it at an efficiency of about 1e-7 to 3e-7 (slowdown 1e6-1e7 at kimi-k2-1m-raw).
claims.next: Prove the partial-sum lemma on the reference circuit and restate incompressibility in bits (support); price the construction over the attacker's boundary codes.

claims.statement: Under the policy, with one registration phase up front, pretraining a new model is slowed by the one-declaration factor across any number of declarations, and the model it produces can't be served without paying about the same factor again (it was never registered).
claims.next: Prove the composition lemma; fix the registered set's budgets; decide whether any re-registration channel exists, since every such channel is a recommitment route and must be slow and priced.

claims.statement: Every catalogued training method is either throttled by at least the floor or has not been shown to produce broad capability gains.
claims.next: Grow the library; run the learning-rule bake-off redesigned to score multiplier x boundary bits.

claims.statement: Translated into capability and time: a year of the world's compute under the policy buys what seconds to minutes of it buy today (a lag of several years of compute growth).
claims.next: State it on the pretraining-loss axis as a lag (a world-year buys a Llama-1-7B to Llama-3-70B class base model); treat capability bought with free inference as its own axis.

claims.statement: Any method that teaches a model frontier-scale new capability must integrate far more than K bits per block, so every learner is throttled, not only today's.
claims.next: An information-theoretic argument for teaching versus elicitation; memory- and communication-sample trade-offs as the tool.

premises.statement: K and Gamma are set by the longest supported session: K = 2e7 bits, Gamma = 6.4e16 at kimi-k2-1m-raw.
A declaration divided into sessions reading only theta and their prompts complies.
Under threading, weight incompressibility and containment, slowdown >= kappa b_a / (2 alpha Lambda).

A small subcircuit of the reference circuit reads b_w bits per updated weight it uses and b_a per thread value. Stated over wiring; proofs recommends the support form. False at step 0 and for small-batch reference circuits.

The reference circuit is (d, e)-threaded with d the entry fee and e the fan-out. Lean derives only (1, 0)-threading from structure; with a committed corpus layer 1 needs no thread reads, and the unembedding needs e >= vocabulary.
The declared circuit contains the reference circuit gate for gate (Declaration.Contains).
slowdown.search: blocks cover slices of a token's computation; never run; omits gradient aggregation and attention reads.
Literature rates for weights, activations, updates and tokens.
Efficiency is read on held-out loss through a Chinchilla law; past the stall it is 1/rho within about 10%, and the choice of law moves it at most 1.6x.

A Hong-Kung / Loomis-Whitney law on the reference circuit (the chain proof's partial-sum charge through Contains): proven ceiling about 3.6e-7 at the 1-year mark. Round 2: per declaration only; about 1,500-3,000 Lean lines; a coded crossing charged soundly gives rho >= 2e4.

Everything committed is registered once, before monitoring, and reused by every declaration; nothing computed under monitoring ever enters theta. So a value one declaration passes to another is novel, and a run split across declarations is charged like one declaration whose theta is the registered set. A short composition lemma (the union of declarations over one registered theta is a declaration) states this in Lean.
Two public budgets on theta (matrix-weight bits and other bits), checked inside the proof so no architecture is revealed.
The algorithm library: 71 algorithms with traits and measured multipliers; queries give a bracket and the read breakdown.
Learning with bounded memory or communication needs more samples (memory-sample and communication lower bounds).

attacks.title: Recommitting theta makes the throttle per declaration
attacks.mechanism: Theta has no provenance or cadence rule. Commit a checkpoint, train a block's worth reading only theta, emit a gradient, recommit. Even daily release lets blocks take hundreds of local steps (DiLoCo-style) from committed weights.
attacks.effect: efficiency 0.3-1 if theta could be refreshed; closed by one registration phase, except through any re-registration channel the policy later allows

attacks.title: The theorem charges values, not bits
attacks.mechanism: Packing a crossing into a few wide values, or deriving operands from theta, slips under the per-value charge.
attacks.repair: Restate incompressibility in bits (support form) and charge coded crossings soundly.

attacks.title: Boundary width is the attacker's choice
attacks.mechanism: Subspace-confined residuals cut a crossing about 140x at 1T; joint coding may cut more until the per-step optimizer-state floor.
attacks.effect: achievable efficiency rises from about 1e-7 to about 1e-5 (one group's results to 8.6B)
attacks.repair: Measure boundary rate-distortion at scale; price the construction over codes.

attacks.title: Threading is unproven for any transformer and false as instantiated
attacks.mechanism: Layer 1 needs no thread reads when the corpus is committed; the unembedding needs e >= vocabulary.
attacks.effect: the blue line is a conditional estimate; repaired, within about 1.1x at 1e28
attacks.repair: Derive threading from the circuit; drop products computable from theta.

attacks.title: Most of the band is the theorem's slack
attacks.mechanism: The thread theorem never charges partial sums, so its ceiling loosens as models widen.
attacks.effect: the true one-declaration value is about 1e-7 to 3e-7, a 2.3x bracket

attacks.title: The construction omits reads
attacks.mechanism: Gradient aggregation and attention reads are not charged.
attacks.repair: Add aggregation and attention to slowdown.search.

attacks.title: The bound covers one literal recipe
attacks.mechanism: Contains embeds one recipe gate for gate; equivalent re-wirings (re-association, Strassen, recompute) escape it; recipe choice moves the theorem 2-4x.
attacks.repair: State the guarantee for a class of recipes.

attacks.title: A declared gate is not a chip-second
attacks.mechanism: size is unweighted and blind to width.

attacks.title: Committed data silences the theorem and frees small models
attacks.mechanism: With the corpus in theta, Contains fails; budgets bound but don't close smuggling (a one-hot activation copies any theta entry; checkpoint slack holds about 2e11 tokens).
attacks.effect: small-model training at efficiency about 1 up to about 1e16 FLOP
attacks.repair: p-theta-budgets, and a theorem with a term for committed data.

attacks.title: Loss is not capability, and inference is free
attacks.mechanism: Search, test-time compute and tiny-update RL buy capability back in verifiable domains.
attacks.effect: capability-matched efficiency x10-1000; x1-3 on knowledge-bound tasks
attacks.repair: Keep the pretraining claim on the loss axis; measure the inference-for-training exchange.

attacks.title: Seed-based post-training fits in a block
attacks.mechanism: A seed pool's decoding fits under Gamma, and under the 11 MB policy every seed row does.
attacks.repair: Measure seed methods' capability ceiling; price decoding in gates.

attacks.title: In-block families beat the stall at mid scale
attacks.mechanism: Routing over small experts, retrieval, recursion and test-time training stay inside blocks.
attacks.effect: x6-150 between 1e23 and 3e25; x1 at frontier loss
attacks.repair: Add them to the library and measure.

attacks.title: Padding is free compute
attacks.mechanism: Padding gates can do theta-only work: data curation, rephrasing, distillation from committed teachers.

attacks.title: Calibration capture
attacks.mechanism: K is set by the most permissive session: long text, video tokens, embedding inputs.
attacks.effect: K x12 for 10M-token text, x600 for video, vacuous for embeddings
attacks.repair: Charge non-text inputs as activations; prefer entropy-coded prompts.

attacks.title: A few bits elicit a lot
attacks.mechanism: Every demonstrated small-update gain elicits latent skill; the policy caps new information, not what it unlocks.
attacks.repair: Claim 'no new base models plus a bounded overhang', not 'no progress'.

attacks.title: Generic lower bounds hit known barriers
attacks.mechanism: Much stronger generic round lower bounds would separate P from NC1, so no proof covers every algorithm.
attacks.effect: claims about all learners need structure
attacks.repair: Bound classes of learners; price what lies outside.

plans.title: Hong-Kung law on the reference circuit
plans.note: Per declaration only; 1,500-3,000 Lean lines; coded crossings need a sound charge (rho >= 2e4).

plans.title: One closed form, rho = c b_a sqrt(b_w) Gamma / K^1.5
plans.note: Algebra holds; 'constant in N' fails for coded crossings.

plans.title: The bound without a named assumption
plans.note: Coding prices an entry at w/d; one step per declaration certifies nothing.

plans.title: Escape routes priced under a square root
plans.note: Recommitment lowers the in-block floor to 1.92 at one per day; activation compression enters linearly.

plans.title: Boundary rate-distortion at scale
plans.note: Judge at the attacker's best multiplier x width; it measures achievable, not the proven ceiling.

plans.title: Learning-rule bake-off
plans.note: Scores extra compute as a cost the policy gives free; misses the round-1 escapes.

plans.title: The NCI meter
plans.note: Add a multi-declaration mode with a theta ledger and output metering; sweep release interval and ledger price (about 2,000 H100-hours).

plans.title: A red-team bounty
plans.note: Grants too small for tier-1 attempts; recommitment fits no tier.
